summary.intent: Decide whether to release the regenerated release PR #396 (and run the oracle) by verifying performance and release-readiness after #466 merged, while also routing blocking findings on the tsrs module-resolution swap PR #467.
summary.outcome: Perf comparison showed no regression from #466 (under noisy machine load), so nothing blocks releasing #396; the unverified stripped Linux/zig release build remains. Three real blocking findings on #467 were routed to the swap worker for a fix with a boundary test matrix.

repo: Callisto regenerates the release PR (#396) after merges to main; its body reflects newly merged changes, and it shows BLOCKED while Entire Gates approval is pending.

`strip = "symbols"` (#454) only runs in the release workflow (callisto-release.yml), which builds darwin arm64/x64 and Linux x64/arm64 (arm64 cross-built with zig) with fail-fast: true, so strip was only verified on macOS and a failure could leave a partial release.
The identity gate fixtures (Chakra-only, gate-large) have no project-internal symlinks, CJS importers, or relative tsconfig paths, so they cannot catch tsrs vs oxc_resolver contract differences.

tsrs_module differs from oxc_resolver in three ways: forward-slash/non-canonical relative symlink paths, importer mode (always `import` condition, dropping `require` for .cts importers), and relative tsconfig paths resolved against `/`.
`oxc_resolver` must stay because `resolve_ts_lib_paths` uses it, so the tsrs swap (#467) deletes 207 lines but adds 378 and shrinks the binary only 34 KB.
getPropertiesOfType is 57% of checker time; the biggest remaining lever is a slimmer upstream entry point from tsrs.
Perf measurement harness: `gate_harness` example with `first-answer` and `watch` subcommands; `caliper-docgen extract --no-cache [--no-checker]` timed with `/usr/bin/time -l`.

code.finding: Three blocking regressions from the tsrs swap: non-canonical symlink paths miss project declarations (High), all importers resolved with `import` condition (Medium), and relative tsconfig names resolved against `/` (Medium).

workflow: Machine load above 100 (other projects' monokl builds plus own rustc) made timings meaningless; gate the benchmark on load <= 8 and record load per line with interleaved old/new runs.
Identical output on a few fixtures is insufficient proof for a dependency swap; boundary tests must target contract differences and fail on the old code before passing.
Delegate fixes to a worker with a call cap, batch all findings together, and verify in source before resolving findings with `entire trail finding resolve` citing commit and test.
Run long benchmarks as background tasks writing to a file instead of polling.

friction: Machine load stayed at 9–14 even after waiting, making absolute timings 1.3–1.5x slower than earlier calm runs and unusable for the speed-lead-over-RDT claim.
First-answer budget (150 ms) passes in quiet runs but fails under load; single runs swing 137–194 ms for the same build.
The one watch-gate pair ran non-interleaved under rising load (p95 234 vs 190 ms) and is inconclusive.
The swap worker hit its call cap before the checker lane finished, and the earlier acceptance of 'identical in all four cases' missed the three regressions.
Finding show required the --branch flag to read findings on #467.
open_items: Verify stripped Linux x64/arm64 (zig) release builds; they can't be tested locally and the publish ordering under fail-fast hasn't been read.
Rerun performance on a quiet machine to confirm the speed lead over RDT and repeat the watch gate interleaved.

Fix the three blocking findings on #467, add tsconfig `references` coverage, and make the watch-invalidation test demonstrably fail on a stale resolver; the worker's checker lane result is still pending.
Decide on F8 (dependency-index cache slower than no cache: 88.4 ms vs 79.5 ms), plus optional F15 (canonical writer serializes props twice, ~3–6 ms) and C2 list sharing (~21 ms).
Never measured: PGO, and the watch budget (ButtonProps p95 ~134 ms vs 25 ms, a docs decision).
Live upgrade has not been watched in a real browser under `storybook dev`.
File the upstream tsrs issue for a slimmer getPropertiesOfType entry point (user action).
User still needs to approve Entire Gates on #396 and decide on releasing and running the oracle.
